Huisman-Weissing multispecies competition system

Source: R/multispecies_competition.R
multispecies_competition.Rd

Creates a Huisman-Weissing resource competition system whose basin boundaries can exhibit fractal structure and Wada-like unpredictability in species outcomes.

Usage

multispecies_competition(
  scenario = c("5species", "8species"),
  dilution = 0.25,
  supply = c(10, 10, 10),
  t_invade = 1000,
  N_invade = 0.1
)

Arguments

scenario

Character. Competition scenario: "5species" specifies 5 species competing for 3 resources, producing 2 possible outcomes (binary basin structure); "8species" specifies 8 species with invasion, producing 3+ possible outcomes suitable for Wada detection.

dilution

Numeric. Resource dilution rate \(D\) (default 0.25 d\(^{-1}\)).

supply

Numeric vector. Resource supply concentrations \(S_j\) (default c(10, 10, 10) \(\mu\)mol L\(^{-1}\)).

t_invade

Numeric. For 8-species scenario, time when species 6-8 invade (default 1000 days).

N_invade

Numeric. Initial abundance of invading species (default 0.1).

Value

A list (system object) containing:

system

"huisman_weissing" string identifier

params

List of all model parameters (K, C, r, m, D, S, etc.)

attractors

List of outcome-based attractor specifications

projection

Named vector indicating which species to vary for 2D basin computation (default: N2 and N4)

scenario

The scenario name

type

"competition"

description

Human-readable description

Details

The Huisman-Weissing model describes \(n\) species competing for \(k\) resources in a chemostat. The dynamics are governed by:

Species dynamics: $$\frac{dN_i}{dt} = N_i \left( \mu_i(R_1, \ldots, R_k) - m_i \right)$$

Resource dynamics: $$\frac{dR_j}{dt} = D(S_j - R_j) - \sum_{i=1}^{n} c_{ji} \mu_i N_i$$

Growth rate (Liebig's law with Monod kinetics): $$\mu_i = \min_{j} \left( r_i \frac{R_j}{K_{ji} + R_j} \right)$$

where \(N_i\) is the abundance of species \(i\), \(R_j\) is the concentration of resource \(j\), \(\mu_i\) is the specific growth rate of species \(i\), \(m_i\) is the mortality rate of species \(i\), \(D\) is the dilution rate, \(S_j\) is the supply concentration of resource \(j\), \(K_{ji}\) is the half-saturation constant of species \(i\) for resource \(j\), \(c_{ji}\) is the resource content (consumption coefficient), and \(r_i\) is the maximum growth rate.

The key finding of Huisman & Weissing is that when \(n > k\) (more species than resources), the system can exhibit chaotic dynamics and fractal basin boundaries. Small changes in initial conditions can lead to completely different community compositions.

5-species scenario:

Five species compete for 3 resources, producing two possible outcomes: either species {1, 2, 3} survive (Outcome 1) or species {1, 4, 5} survive (Outcome 2). The basin boundary between these outcomes is fractal.

8-species scenario:

Eight species compete, with species 6, 7, 8 invading at \(t = 1000\) days. This produces three distinct outcomes based on which invader dominates: species 6 (Outcome 1), species 7 (Outcome 2), or species 8 (Outcome 3). With 3+ outcomes, the system can exhibit Wada basin boundaries.

References

Huisman, J., & Weissing, F. J. (2001). Fundamental unpredictability in multispecies competition. American Naturalist, 157(5), 488-494. doi:10.1086/319929

Huisman, J., & Weissing, F. J. (1999). Biodiversity of plankton by species oscillations and chaos. Nature, 402(6760), 407-410. doi:10.1038/46540

See also

compute_competition_basins for computing basins, forced_damped_pendulum for comparison with physical systems, wada_merging_method for Wada detection.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# ===================================================================== #
# Example 1: 5-species competition (fractal boundary, not Wada)         #
# ===================================================================== #
hw5 <- multispecies_competition(scenario = "5species")
print(hw5$description)

# Compute basins varying initial N2 and N4
basins5 <- compute_competition_basins(hw5, c(0, 2), c(0, 2),
                                      resolution = 200)
plot(basins5, title = "5-species competition basins")

# ===================================================================== #
# Example 2: 8-species competition (potential Wada basins)              #
# ===================================================================== #
hw8 <- multispecies_competition(scenario = "8species")
basins8 <- compute_competition_basins(hw8, c(0, 2), c(0, 2),
                                      resolution = 200)
plot(basins8, title = "8-species competition basins")

# Test for Wada property
result <- wada_merging_method(basins8)
print(result)

# ===================================================================== #
# Example 3: Custom parameters                                          #
# ===================================================================== #
hw_custom <- multispecies_competition(scenario = "5species",
                                      dilution = 0.3,
                                      supply = c(12, 8, 10))
} # }
